question.prompt: Tom, Dick, and Harry are playing a game. Starting at the same time, each of them flips a fair coin repeatedly until he gets his first head, at which point he stops. What is the probability that all three flip their coins the same number of times?

solutions.explanation:
For one player to stop on flip \(n\ge1\), his first \(n-1\) flips must be tails and his next flip must be heads. By independence, this has probability
\[
\left(\frac12\right)^{n-1}\frac12
=\left(\frac12\right)^n.
\]
The three players' flips are independent, so the probability that all three stop on flip \(n\) is
\[
\left(\left(\frac12\right)^n\right)^3
=\left(\frac18\right)^n.
\]
Different common stopping flips give mutually exclusive events, and they cover every successful outcome. Also, endless flipping has probability zero, since the probability of \(n\) initial tails is \(2^{-n}\), which tends to zero.

We therefore add the probabilities over \(n=1,2,\ldots\). This is a convergent geometric series with first term and common ratio both \(1/8\):
\[
P=\frac18+\frac1{8^2}+\frac1{8^3}+\cdots
=\frac{1/8}{1-1/8}
=\boxed{\frac17}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
solutions.title: Sum over the common stopping flip

solutions.explanation:
Let \(p\) be the probability that the three first heads occur on the same flip. Examine the first round, in which all three players flip once.

If all three get heads, they stop together immediately. This has probability \((1/2)^3=1/8\).

If all three get tails, also with probability \(1/8\), everyone continues. Their future flips are independent of the first round. Everyone has used one flip, so whether their final totals agree depends only on the future flips, exactly as at the start. Their remaining chance of success is therefore \(p\).

In every mixed outcome, some players stop after one flip while others need at least two flips. Their totals can never all agree, so these outcomes contribute zero.

These cases are disjoint and exhaustive, giving
\[
p=\frac18+\frac18p.
\]
Solving,
\[
\frac78p=\frac18,
\qquad p=\boxed{\frac17}.
\]
Thus the answer is choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
